items.problem: router2 (major): redirectAddress filled a ':name' from any parameter in the redirect's full path, parent routes included. Angular binds only the redirect route's own match and throws 4001 otherwise, so the extractor drew a false must (for example /p/7/x -> /q/:id).
items.what: Redirect now carries `relative` (redirectTo has no leading slash) and `own` (how many segments the route's own path declares). The signature is redirectAddress(address, at, to, own, relative). It binds `:name` only from the last `own` segments of `at`. A relative target takes the parent's segments from the address. A catch-all binds nothing and consumes any number of segments. A name left unbound returns null, and land() then returns target null with unread set: no edge, plus a dynamic-target note. An empty-path child's redirect (RouteInfo.redirectsTo is now a Redirect) also goes through redirectAddress with own = 0. Before this change an absolute '' child redirect naming a parent parameter was followed as must; now it lands nowhere, and the host screen gets no edge either. Unreadable function targets keep the old rule: the landing stays on the target and is ambiguous. Authority is @angular/router 18.2.14 fesm2022/router.mjs. applyRedirectCommands is at :3567-3580. findPosParam throws 4001 at :3614-3620. expandSegmentAgainstRouteUsingRedirect calls match() for the redirect route alone at :3902 and passes only its positionalParamSegments at :3922. match() is at :3651-3686. createWildcardMatchResult returns positionalParamSegments {} at :3687-3695.

items.problem: router2 (major): land() followed a second redirect after a relative one. Angular re-enters the redirect's own table with allowRedirects=false, so a redirect there is skipped (NoMatch). The new parameter-pattern branch had extended this false must.
items.what: land() remembers the redirect applied at the previous hop (`prev`). After a relative one, the next answer must pass the new within(): its chain shares every route above the relative redirect route, so its route there belongs to the same table. At the root that table is the joined ROUTES (router.mjs:5298 flattens them). A redirect answer must also sit below a route of that table, because a child table is processed with redirects on (:3967) while the table itself is re-entered with them off (:3896-3899, :3924). If either check fails, the walk stops with target null and unread set: no edge, plus a dynamic-target note. This also closes a pre-existing false must: a relative redirect whose target screen sits under a different parent route with the same path (two 'p' routes). A redirect record that says no place (the merged full plus prefix record, levels []) also stops the walk. A redirect met after an ABSOLUTE redirect now makes the landing ambiguous (may). Angular 18 rematches from the root with redirects on (:3579, :3797-3799). Before 18 the router applied no redirect after an absolute one. This rests on the v18 changelog's breaking change ('Absolute redirects no longer prevent further redirects'), not on source, because no Angular 16 or 17 router is installed. k8sdash runs 16.2.1, and the extractor does not read the version. The doc comments on land() and within() say so.

report.approximationsForThesis:
Exact sentence for the approximation list (ch6 §Declared approximations): "A catch-all route (`**`) declared in a route table that the application registers separately, through its own ROUTES provider as a forChild call or a dedicated wildcard routing module registers it, is assumed to be matched after every route of the application's other tables, because the extractor does not read the order in which the tables are registered; whenever it relies on this assumption the extractor emits a route-order note for the application naming the catch-all, and on the corpus the 125 must edges of k8sdash and the one of bitwarden rest on it."

- A redirect after an absolute redirect is held at may, because the extractor does not read the Angular version and versions before 18 apply no further redirect.
- A redirect naming a parameter its own route does not bind, or one met after a relative redirect in that redirect's own table, yields no edge and a dynamic-target note.
- An unmatched address goes to the deepest catch-all at may.

items.what: The rule now lives in one place, outletHiddenAbove (attribute.ts). It answers per (screen, component). It reads the screen's chain of routes off route.levels: each level's holder is its layout, its minted route's component, or the component a wrapper's route names (callMount(...).route, e.g. mifos withShell's ShellComponent). The component is hidden on that screen when any holder above its own place does not render its primary outlet firmly. Firm means: the holder's own template holds the outlet outside every template condition, or, where it holds none, it firmly places a component that renders one firmly. That nested scan uses nestingGraph restricted to the holder's template (new optional `only` parameter). It covers ghostfolio's pages, which hold no outlet of their own and render it through <gf-page-tabs>, and mifos's Shell, which renders it through <mifosx-content>. Four cases are taken as hidden, the safe side: no outlet found at all, a level whose route names a component the reader cannot resolve, a component missing from the chain, and a component that places itself. Three places use it: the per-route loop (replacing behindHiddenOutlet), the descendants loop in extract.ts (which now splits each component's screens into sure and unsure and emits the unsure ones as conditional), and attributeScopes, whose firm nesting now descends only from the screens where the route component or layout is firm, so a component it nests is conditional where it is. Angular authority: router.mjs 2659-2680. An outlet inside an NgIf creates the routed component only when the outlet itself is instantiated.

report.approximationsForThesis:
Add to the declared-approximations list (ch6 sec:approximations, in-scope group) the outlet rule, worded as follows:

"Whether a component renders on every execution of a screen is decided from the outlets above it on that screen's chain of routes: the outlet a route component, a layout or a wrapper's shell renders in its own template, or, where its template holds none, through a component it places outside every template condition. An outlet that a template places inside another component's element is taken to render whenever that template does, and so is an outlet reached through a selector that several components match (the ambiguous-selector note records the latter in the attributed graph). An outlet the reader cannot find at all, and a component it cannot resolve, hide everything below them."

The extractor emits no new note for the projection assumption. It is the same assumption the site-condition reader already makes for every site placed inside a component's content, with only mat-menu and mat-tab listed as lazy. Ambiguous selectors are covered by the existing ambiguous-selector note.

No other residual assumption is introduced. Every other uncertain case is resolved to the safe side:
- no outlet found: hidden
- unresolved holder: hidden
- canMatch on an empty-path child: not a layout
- a later empty-path child: not a layout
- a componentless route with canMatch: does not hold its address

If (a) under corpusImpact stays open, the list must also carry this sentence:

"A route that carries a canMatch, and any later route at the same address, is taken to render its own component there whenever the screen is shown, although Angular may skip the canMatch route or reach the later one (router.mjs 3641-3650); no edge of the corpus's must tier rests on this."

problems.where: packages/adapter-angular/src/routes.ts:1049-1053 (host branch) feeding attribute.ts outletHiddenAbove (chain = route.levels.map(holderOf))
problems.what: NEW false must. When the first empty-path child under a screen is reached through a wrapper call (`children: [withShell([...])]`, `children: withShell([...])`, `[...withShell([...])]`, or a lazy table holding such a call), the wrapper's own route object never goes through the host branch. The inner child H is the one appended to host.layouts. But `host.levels` gets only `levels[levels.length-1]` (H's level), so the screen's chain is [X, H] and is missing the wrapper's Shell level. outletHiddenAbove never sees Shell's outlet, and the `level.canMatch` check never sees a canMatch on the wrapper's route. H's links on the host screen come out at must even though Angular renders H only inside Shell's outlet, and only when the wrapper's route matches. On main, H was unplaced (o_H, may).
problems.evidence: Scratch probe on the worktree source vs 9938dc6. Routes `function withShell(children){ return { path: '', component: Shell, children } }; [{ path: 'x', component: X, children: [withShell([{ path: '', component: H }])] }, { path: 'p', component: P }]`. X is `<router-outlet>`, Shell is `@if (on) { <router-outlet> }`, H is `<a routerLink="/p">`. Worktree: ['n_x>n_p:must'] from h.component.ts. Main: ['o_H>n_p:may']. Angular processSegment (router.mjs 3859-3876) matches Shell '' and then H '', so H sits inside Shell's outlet. Fix: append every level from the host's depth onward (the wrapper levels included) to host.levels, or skip the layouts append when any level between host and child is a wrapper level or carries a canMatch.
